channel.title: Wisper Note — Changelog
channel.description: Every release, what changed, and what we broke. Written the day it shipped.

item.title: Launch lane — Preview download, role-based disclosures, billing built
item.description: Development, not a release. The macOS Preview download went live on this site with its SHA-256 beside it. Every disclosure on the site and in the app now describes each processor by what it does rather than by supplier, which is why the privacy policy's effective date and the terms' last-updated date moved to 2026-09-24. Sign-in, the free weekly cap and Pro checkout are built and unit-tested but switched off until the account service is provisioned. Known issues: Whether a quarantined, ad-hoc-signed download is offered Open Anyway on macOS 15 and 26 has not been tested from a browser download. Accounts, the cap and Pro have not run end to end: there is no hosted account service yet.

Release notes only; this version has no download. Added: First public macOS build (Apple silicon). Hold ⌥ Space, speak, let go. Today pane: words, dictations and estimated minutes saved for the past seven days, with the formula shown. History as a day-grouped timeline, 100 entries a page, with copy, raw transcript, dictionary and delete on every entry. Light theme by default, dark theme from the switch at the bottom of the sidebar. Changed: The sidebar groups the product panes at the top and pins Account, Privacy, Settings, Advanced and Help to the bottom. Every disclosure describes the transcription, cleanup and storage services by what they do rather than by supplier. Known issues: Preview build: the speech service is not connected yet, so a dictation replays a sample transcript and is marked Sample. It shows the app; it does not yet transcribe you. Typing into other apps is not connected in this build. The result goes to your clipboard and the pill tells you to press ⌘V. Not signed with an Apple Developer ID and not notarized (ad-hoc signature only). The first open goes through System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway; tested from a browser download on macOS 26.5 on 2026-09-25 (the button appears). macOS 15 untested. Apple silicon only. There is no Intel build. There is no auto-update. A new version is a new download.

Sample transcripts are labelled Sample, and the Today pane says plainly when a build has no transcription service. Changed: Nothing in the app names the services it runs on; each is described by what it does. The download is served as a file from wispernote.com with its SHA-256 beside it. item.title: 0.1.5 — macOS
item.description: Release for macOS. Changed: Signing in from the app now gives the app a session of its own: the website hands over a single-use key instead of its own sign-in, so the two never interfere. A sign-in that launched the app from the link is recognised for fifteen minutes after a restart. item.title: Sprint 0 — foundation, research, spec freeze
item.description: Development, not a release. The monorepo, the seven architecture decisions behind it, two de-risking spikes, a hello-world on every one of the six surfaces, the frozen spec, and a placeholder page live on the domain. No product code that a person could use yet. Known issues: The iPhone keyboard handoff — keyboard extension to URL scheme to host app to shared container and back — is unproven until the simulator spike runs. The macOS Accessibility grant for a development build is a manual step in System Settings, so the injection spike and the end-to-end test cannot run without a person clicking it. Windows is only verifiable in continuous integration. There is no local Windows machine. The product name and the domain are both spelled without an h — Wisper Note, wispernote.com — and the owner has not yet ruled on whether that stays. Chrome Web Store developer registration has not been completed, and the extension cannot be submitted until it is. The website deploy script needs its credentials resolvable from the environment or the keychain, never from the repository.
